anti_patterns: Single-operator oracle feeding high-value settlement without aggregation or dispute path: one compromised key or API rewrites every downstream payout
Consuming latestAnswer without checking updatedAt round timestamp: a stale feed past its heartbeat silently prices loans and liquidations off old data
Reading price feeds on L2 without consulting the L2 sequencer uptime feed: sequencer outage leaves consumers acting on frozen values
One source, many nodes: a network of operators all polling the same API inherits that API's outage and manipulation as if it were centralized
Pushing every observation onchain instead of offchain aggregation: N operator transactions per round burns gas the OCR single-report design exists to avoid
Treating blockhash or block timestamp as randomness: miners and builders control both, so outcomes are grindable; use VRF proofs instead
Hardcoding feed proxy addresses without an upgrade path: aggregator migrations strand consumers pinned to deprecated contracts
avoid_when: All required state already lives onchain and no external input is needed
Sub-second update latency is mandatory; oracle rounds and dispute windows add seconds to minutes
The deployment cannot tolerate any external trust assumption, however diluted
Data changes so frequently that per-update verification gas exceeds the value secured
A single trusted operator is acceptable; a signed API response is simpler and cheaper
Answers are subjective or non-attributable with no quorum or dispute procedure able to settle them
best_practices: Read through the proxy (AggregatorV3Interface.latestRoundData) rather than the aggregator directly so aggregator upgrades do not strand consumers
Gate every consumption on freshness: check updatedAt/latestTimestamp against the feed heartbeat and pause or fall back when stale
On L2, check the sequencer uptime feed alongside the price answer and enter a grace mode during outages
Decentralize both layers: multiple independent data sources and multiple independent node operators, never one source behind many nodes
Prefer offchain aggregation (OCR-style single report carrying all observations and signatures) to minimize per-round gas
Require signed, attributable observations so operator history can be audited and misbehavior slashed
For randomness, verify the VRF proof onchain before any consumer logic touches the value; fund subscription accounts ahead of demand spikes
For pull/on-demand reads, preflight with simulation so OracleDataRequired reverts resolve into the same atomic multicall
Plan feed migration: track typeAndVersion and proxy configuration so aggregator replacements do not break consumers
benefits: Breaks the determinism barrier: contracts consume market prices, weather, randomness, and cross-chain state they could never fetch natively
Multi-layer aggregation (sources, then nodes, then network median) removes single points of failure at both data and operator layers
Offchain reporting compresses a full aggregation round into one onchain transaction, cutting per-update gas by up to 90 percent versus per-operator submission
Verifiable randomness (VRF proof checked onchain before use) gives manipulation-resistant unpredictability no block variable can offer
Standard interfaces (AggregatorV3Interface, ERC-2362 valueFor, ERC-7412 fulfillOracleQuery) make oracle providers interchangeable and combinable via medianizers and routers
Proxy-behind-aggregator deployment lets feed implementations upgrade without interrupting consumers
Staking, signed observations, and dispute windows make data attributable and accountable: honest reporting is rewarded, false reporting is slashable
On-demand pull (revert-and-multicall) scales to L2/L3 execution contexts where pushing every feed everywhere is uneconomical
component_types: Oracle Nodes: offchain clients that fetch source data, sign observations, and run aggregation protocols (Flux Monitor, OCR, OCR2, VRF jobs)
Data Sources: external APIs, aggregators, and attestors (market venues, reserve auditors, weather stations) polled by nodes
Aggregator Contract: onchain contract receiving periodic updates and storing the latest aggregated answer for same-transaction reads
Proxy Contract: stable onchain address forwarding consumer calls to the current aggregator across upgrades
Consumer Contract: any contract reading the feed via AggregatorV3Interface.latestRoundData or ERC-2362 valueFor
Coordinator / Verifier: VRF coordinator or ERC-7412 oracle contract verifying proofs and caching data for subsequent calls
Dispute / Staking Module: bonds, votes, and challenge windows attributing answers to reporters and punishing falsehoods
Automation Keeper Network: DON monitoring time and event conditions and submitting wake-up transactions when upkeep is due
context: Smart contracts execute deterministically and can only read onchain state, yet lending, derivatives, insurance, prediction markets, gaming, and automation depend on offchain facts: asset prices, reserve balances, weather events, election outcomes, randomness, and cross-chain state. The oracle pattern bridges this gap with a dedicated subsystem of offchain collector nodes plus onchain anchor contracts that source, verify, aggregate, and deliver external data to consuming contracts in a tamper-resistant, attributable way, so thousands of replaying nodes can share one verified input without breaking consensus.
design_principles: Determinism Preservation: external data enters only as finalized onchain state, never as ambient I/O during execution
Multi-Layer Decentralization: no single source, operator, RPC endpoint, or network configuration is load-bearing
Attributability and Accountability: every observation is signed and bonded so reporters can be rewarded or slashed
Verify Before Consume: proofs (VRF), quorum signatures (OCR), and dispute windows resolve before consumers act
Minimal Onchain Footprint: aggregate offchain, publish one report; store answers, not raw observations
Freshness as Correctness: timestamps and heartbeats are part of the answer; stale data is invalid data
Interchangeability: standard pull/push interfaces let consumers combine or swap providers without rewriting logic
name: oracle-pattern

technology_stack: Chainlink VRF v2.5 (subscription and direct-funding) and Automation
Maker Oracles Medianizer and Schelling-point median aggregation
Pyth and Redstone pull-based price updates with onchain signature verification
Witnet decentralized oracle network with algorithmic reputation
ERC-2362 valueFor pull interface, ERC-7412 revert-and-multicall retrieval, ERC-3668 CCIP-Read
tradeoffs: Added trust surface: consumers inherit the oracle network's honesty threshold, so a corrupted quorum corrupts every dependent contract
Latency overhead: aggregation rounds, deviation/heartbeat triggers, and dispute windows add seconds to minutes versus native reads
Gas cost per update: each published answer is an onchain transaction, bounding feasible update frequency and payload size
Staleness risk: consumers must independently enforce freshness (updatedAt, heartbeats, sequencer health) or act on frozen data during outages
Source-correlation fragility: operators polling the same upstream API share its failure and manipulation modes despite node-level redundancy
MEV and front-running around predictable feed updates (oracle-extractable value) unless mitigated with auctions or commit-reveal
Operational complexity: running nodes, funding VRF subscriptions, tracking proxy upgrades, and monitoring deviations is a standing DevOps burden
use_cases: DeFi price feeds securing lending, perpetuals, and stablecoin collateral via medianized multi-operator answers
Proof of Reserve attestations verifying stablecoin and wrapped-asset backing onchain
Parametric crop insurance paying out when oracle-quorum weather data confirms drought or flood thresholds
Prediction markets settling election and sports outcomes through staked-vote oracle resolution
Onchain gaming and NFT mints drawing manipulation-resistant randomness from VRF proofs
L2 sequencer uptime feeds gating liquidations and trading during sequencer outages
Cross-chain reads via ERC-7412 on-demand retrieval where pushing every feed to every rollup is uneconomical
Automated keepers (liquidations, limit orders, rebalancing) triggered by DON-monitored time and event conditions
